note: Recorded 2026-11-02 19:14 with the live AI investigator (claude-code:sonnet) on a local instance. The engineer's messages are scripted for this demo (not from the original issue thread); Veyra's replies are the model's real output.

payload.message: I think the agent is the problem. Port 457879 is invalid, so the agent drops the session, and after that the board just retries forever.

steps.label: Read the report and earlier results
Decoded every packet in the log

result.reply: The data disagrees on the port: the agent wrapped 457879 to 64663 and the session was established, so the port isn't why it closed. The agent also didn't drop it on its own; it received 36 zero bytes and treated them as a delete. After that the agent log shows only identical 13-byte packets arriving, which points at the board side.

parts.claim: Port 457879 is invalid and caused the session to fail.
parts.why: Agent wrapped the port to 64663, then received a create and established the session at 192.168.10.210:38908. The port path worked.

evidence.quote: [1707258509.431443] info     | SessionManager.hpp | establish_session        | session established    | client_key: 0x2A2ED975, address: 192.168.10.210:38908

parts.claim: The agent drops the session on its own, so the agent is the problem.
parts.why: The agent did close the session, but right after receiving a 36-byte all-zero packet, decoded as a delete. The trigger is the received data.

evidence.quote: [1707258509.539626] info     | SessionManager.hpp | destroy_session          | session closed         | client_key: 0x2A2ED975, address: 192.168.10.210:38908

parts.claim: After the close the board retries forever.
parts.why: The agent received identical 13-byte packets about every 0.1 s (lines 18 to 34, nine in the log), not literally forever. The log is short. The retry logic is on the board, which this log can't see.

hypotheses.claim: The micro-ROS client sends a zeroed or uninitialised buffer after session creation, through a stream, buffer size or init bug.
hypotheses.because: The agent received a 36-byte all-zero packet after a valid create, then repeated 13-byte packets with a nonsense header. The board's own transmit data is not observed.

hypotheses.claim: The packet is corrupted or zeroed below the transport callback, for example by H7 cache and DMA coherency or a wrong pbuf.
hypotheses.because: This fits a zeroed payload after a good first packet, but the agent log cannot see the board's stack.

hypotheses.claim: Cable, switch or router corrupts or injects the zero packet.
hypotheses.because: A clean all-zero payload looks unlike line corruption, but only the receiving host was observed.

hypotheses.claim: The micro-ROS agent mishandles a valid message and closes the session wrongly.
hypotheses.because: The agent's delete followed a received all-zero packet. It then logged an invalid client key warning for 0x00000000, which is consistent with that packet.

hypotheses.claim: The out-of-range port 457879 stopped the board and agent from communicating.
hypotheses.because: The agent wrapped the port to 64663 and established a session, so the port path worked.
hypotheses.observed_at: agent host receive and session log

next_check.action: Capture the board's UDP traffic with Wireshark at the switch port.
next_check.why: Shows whether the board transmitted the 36 zero bytes or whether they were zeroed after leaving its application code. This splits firmware from the DMA and network areas.
how: Mirror the board's switch port to a laptop running Wireshark
Compare the 36-byte payload to what the agent logged at line 10

outcomes.label: Capture shows 36 zero bytes on wire
outcomes.means: The zeros left the board, so the fault is upstream of the NIC: firmware or DMA.
outcomes.then: Dump the transport write buffer before the send call.

outcomes.label: Capture shows a non-zero payload
outcomes.means: The packet was changed after leaving the board. This points at the network path or the host receive path.
outcomes.then: Compare captures at the board and at the host NIC.

still_unknown: What the board actually transmitted at the 36-byte send
Whether the board's retry loop ever ends

result.reply: The data doesn't support the switch. A switch forwards frames and would not turn 36 bytes into a clean run of zeros with the length unchanged. Your own tcpdump on the agent PC saw the zeros too, so they were already in the frame when it reached the host. That leaves the board's Tx path, where D-cache and DMA coherency fit best. The switch is weakened, not excluded, because nothing here observes the cable.

parts.claim: The unmanaged switch corrupted the 36-byte packet in transit.
parts.why: Agent log shows 36 bytes, every byte zero, length intact. Line corruption would not give a clean all-zero payload. The switch is not observed, so it is not excluded.
